The Brier score (0.2524) quantifies forecast reliability over 33 settled games. The gap threshold (0.08) acts as a veto mechanism for model-market divergence. These operators form a dual structure: one layer resolves uncertainty via association, while another enforces coherence through premise alignment. Failure modes include interference-induced misalignment and threshold-crossed divergence. The system avoids causal inference by design, relying instead on statistical association and conditional probability.
